deities: Goddess Padmakshi (Lakshmi/Padmavathi - 'Amma'; rock-cut idol carved from the stone)
Jain Tirthankara sculptures including Parshvanatha flanked by Yaksha and Yakshini (heritage layer)
The Annakonda Pillar - quadrangular black-granite column with Jain and Brahmanical carvings at the entrance
festivals: Bathukamma (before Dussehra) - celebrated by women with grand floral arrangements at the sacred pond; the temple's signature festival

history.dynasty: Kakatiya (under Kakatiya chief Prola II; originally Shaivite, later Jain, then Veerashaiva-influenced Hindu)
history.period: Multi-layered: artificial Shaivite caves west of the shrine possibly pre-5th century CE; Jain Kadalalaya-basadi established 1117 CE per inscription; Brahmanical temple post-1156 CE; 19th-century ownership dispute; Nizam land grant 1869
history.summary: One of the oldest temples of the Hanamkonda region, the historic hilltop shrine of 'Amma' dedicated to Goddess Padmakshi (Lakshmi, lotus-eyed). The site's layers span religions: it began as a Shaivite cave temple (artificial caves west of the present structure, possibly carved before the 5th century CE in early Brahmanical style); a Jain shrine was introduced under the Chalukyas of Vatapi or Rashtrakutas; and a dated 1117 CE inscription records the establishment of the Jain Kadalalaya-basadi, commissioned by Mailama, wife of the Kakatiya minister Betana-pergada, with land donated by Medarasa of Ugravadi, during the rule of the Kakatiya chief Prola II (himself a Shaivite). After 1156 CE the Jain shrine gave way to a Brahmanical temple, likely under Veerashaiva influence. In the 19th century the Jains petitioned the Nizam of Hyderabad for the site, but his commission concluded it had originally hosted a Hindu shrine, and land was granted in 1869 CE for the temple's upkeep. Today the Hindu temple of Padmakshi preserves a rich Jain epigraphic and sculptural heritage - Tirthankara carvings including a Parshvanatha with Yaksha-Yakshini attendants, Jain motifs on the black-granite Annakonda Pillar at the entrance, and the 1117 CE inscription - while the rock-cut idol of the Goddess and the hilltop tank below anchor its Shaktism worship. The sacred pond by the hillock is the focal point of Bathukamma celebrations. CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is in HANAMKONDA (Padmakshi Gutta), about 6-8 km from Warangal - CSV town 'Warangal' is approximate. Corrected to Hanamkonda, district Hanamkonda.

name: Padmakshi Temple
town_description: Hanamkonda (Hanamkonda) is the historic twin city of Warangal in Telangana, known for its Thousand Pillar Temple, Warangal Fort and Padmakshi hillock. The temple sits atop the Padmakshi hillock overlooking a sacred tank, with panoramic views of Hanamkonda; some visitors note the premises need better maintenance.
tradition: Hinduism (Shaktism; with a significant Jain heritage layer)

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad - about 150-160 km (verify).
travel.railway: Kazipet Junction and Hanamkonda area stations are the closest (verify).
travel.road: About 6-8 km from Warangal city, near the Thousand Pillar Temple and Warangal Fort; climb the sheet-covered steps to the hilltop sanctum.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Bathukamma (before Dussehra) is the most colourful time to visit.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Opening hours not sourced - verify before visiting; hilltop access is via stone steps so visit in daylight.
